page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; no margin notes except a short mark in the left margin level with the first lines, which is a printed side-mark (the "„" marks) and no note text. Below the text: nothing printed except the stray mark "lic" which is a catchword.

main_text.p: rationibus subiugit Fernelius, ambiguita—te,non uacat. Ait enim cruditate in cache—xia e uiscceribus in pedes incumbentem du—intumescant,podagras no efficere.Cache—ticos sane oportuit Fernelium distingue—re.Etenim non omnibus eadem est articu—lorum natura. Nonnulli namq; firmis sunt articulis, quibus nulla podagra contingere poteft,etiam si totum eorum corpus prauis succis scateat.Alij uero, quibus pedum compagines uel natura,uel morbo,uel deniq; exterioribus causis imbecillae sunt,podagra facile corripi possunt. Coplures certe uidimus,qui simul & cachectici, & podagrici erant.Quare cachecticos nunqua effi—ci podagricos nimis simpliciter asseruit Fernelius.Tande ex falso pronunciato falsam producit conclusionem. Concludit enim nullam aliam esse arthritidis origine, qua exteriores capitis partes, & extra caluam positas, e quibus ait superuacaneum humore per summa corporis sub cute deorsum decurrere. At si uera haec esset conclusio,omnem profecto arthritidis paroxysmum necessario antecederet capitis dolor externus, non solum ab intemperie frigida,sed ab aquae, aut tenuis pituitae copia il—lic

page.notes: Printed side-marks "„" in the left margin at the first lines (lines 1–4) are typographic marks, not note text, so no notes are transcribed. Several words in the scan are faint or smudged (e.g. "contingere", "scateat" and "lic" at the foot); where I am not fully certain of a word I have not marked it, so the reader should check the lines "Cache-xia" and "scateat" against the scan. The catchword "lic" at the foot is the start of the next line ("illic"), printed as the catchword.
